QF.id: AIFM Fund Monitoring, Reporting, and Exit_15

question.text: Purvanchal Special Situations Fund seeks to enter a Dissolution Period after its Liquidation Period expires. Under SEBI's April-2024 framework, the Dissolution Period cannot exceed:

answer.text: The original tenure of the scheme, with no further extension
It is open-ended until all assets are monetised

explanation.text: The Logic: The Dissolution Period follows expiry of the Liquidation Period, requires investor consent, cannot exceed the original tenure of the scheme, and cannot be extended once it commences. The Trap: '1 year' confuses the Dissolution Period with the Liquidation Period. '2 years with 2/3rd consent' repurposes tenure-extension language that does not apply here. 'Open-ended' is wrong — an outer cap is prescribed. Note: Entry into the Dissolution Period also requires filing an information memorandum with a merchant banker's due-diligence certificate, and no fresh commitments or new investments are permitted during this period.
